name: VitVin
tagline: An Argentine wine app for tracking bottles, vintages and tasting records.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip it down and this is a catalog: bottles, producers, vintages, where they sit, when to drink them, what you thought of the last one. That is a CRUD app with photos and a search box, and an agent will produce a working local version before your coffee goes cold. The part you cannot generate is reference data: a clean producer and vintage catalog, label recognition, and regional appellation rules that someone maintained by hand. If VitVin is doing winery-side regulatory reporting rather than personal cellar tracking, the answer flips hard to no, because reporting formats and audit trails are not vibe-codeable. For a personal cellar, type your own bottles in and you are done.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you log bottles with producer, vintage, region, purchase price, storage slot and tasting notes, then search, filter by drink window, and mark bottles as consumed.
requirements: A machine or small VPS to run it on
Patience for typing in your own bottles
whatYouLose: A pre-built catalog of producers, labels and vintages, so every bottle is manual entry
Label photo recognition, if the paid app has it
Anything resembling market pricing or valuation data
Mobile app convenience while standing in a cellar with cold hands
Any compliance or official reporting output, if that is what the product is actually for
moatNotes: Curated wine reference data is slow, boring work that nobody enjoys repeating. If there is a regulatory reporting angle, that is the real lock-in.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because entering four hundred bottles by hand is a punishment, and a product that already knows the producer, the appellation and the typical drinking window turns that into a few taps. People also pay to not think about schema design for a hobby. And if the app sits on the business side, feeding official declarations or traceability records, the price is cheaper than getting the paperwork wrong once.
notes: Thin information on this one, so the verdict covers the personal-cellar reading of the product.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal wine cellar tracker. Empty folder, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/cellar.db, created and migrated on first boot
- No ORM, write plain SQL in a small db module

Data model:
- bottle: id, producer, wine_name, vintage (nullable for NV), country, region, appellation, grape_varieties (text), color (red/white/rose/sparkling/fortified), size_ml (default 750), quantity, storage_location (free text like 'rack B, slot 12'), purchase_date, purchase_price, currency (default ARS), drink_from_year, drink_until_year, label_photo_path, created_at
- tasting: id, bottle_id, tasted_on, score (0-100 nullable), notes, companions (text)
- consumption: id, bottle_id, consumed_on, occasion

Features, in scope:
- Add, edit, delete bottles with a single clean form
- Cellar list view with text search across producer, wine name, region and grapes, plus filters for color, country, vintage range and drink window
- 'Drink now' view: bottles where current year falls inside drink_from_year..drink_until_year, and a separate 'past window' warning list
- Log a tasting against a bottle, with notes and optional score; show tasting history on the bottle page
- Mark bottles consumed, which decrements quantity and writes a consumption row
- Label photo upload stored on disk under ./data/uploads, served through a route handler, thumbnails rendered with next/image
- Dashboard: total bottles, total cellar value by currency, breakdown by color and by country, ten oldest vintages
- CSV import and CSV export of the full bottle table, so nothing is trapped

Out of scope, do not build:
- Any external wine database lookup, label OCR, auth, multi user, or price scraping
- A mobile app; make the web UI usable one handed on a phone browser instead

Also:
- Seed the db with five example bottles so the UI is not empty on first run
- Put any config in .env.local, commit a .env.example, never hardcode paths outside ./data
- README with one install command and one run command, and a one line backup instruction (copy the data folder)
